title: Maximum residue levels for fenpropathrin
summary: EU to reduce MRLs for fenpropathrin on citrus fruits, strawberries, melons, and tea from July 2027
update: The European Union (EU) will reduce the maximum residue levels (MRLs) for fenpropathrin on citrus fruits, strawberries, melons, and tea to the limit of determination (LOD) of 0.01 mg/kg. (The LOD is the lowest level that can be detected using the most modern and reliable analytical methods.) Current LODs on other products will also be reduced.
what_changing: The EU will reduce the MRLs for fenpropathrin as summarised in Table 1.
why: The MRLs for fenpropathrin that have been in place since the adoption of Regulation 396/2005 have never been reviewed. Following a series of evaluations and a stakeholder consultation (see EFSA invites submission of data to support review of certain MRLs ), the European Food Safety Authority was not able to conclude a risk assessment due to inadequate toxicological data ( EFSA 2023 ).
timeline: The new MRLs are expected to apply from July 2027 .
actions: Suppliers to the EU market of citrus fruits, strawberries, melons, and tea should review their existing use of fenpropathrin and start to look for alternative (chemical or non-chemical) solutions in anticipation of the MRL reductions.
background:
MRLs are set in accordance with the rules set out in Regulation 396/2005 . For information on current MRLs for other substances, please consult the EU Pesticide Residues database .

For further information on the EU’s process and principles for setting MRLs, see Regulation of pesticide residues in the EU - Questions and Answers .
resources: EFSA (2023) Targeted review of maximum residue levels (MRLs) for fenpropathrin . EFSA Journal, 21(6): 8057.
